title: Spectral interval
description:
A spectral scan over a depth interval, with the mineral or geounit abundances it resolved.

GENERATED from the normative OpenAPI document (`spec/openapi.yaml`) — do not edit by hand; run `python scripts/regenerate.py`. The OpenAPI document is normative for the wire; this file is the same contract for one record type, readable on its own.
x-generated-by: scripts/regenerate.py from spec/openapi.yaml (geoDB Open Exploration Protocol v0.1.0)

bhid.description: Natural key of the drill hole: `{"hole_id", "project", "company"}`.

scheme.description: Id of the related lookup row. Resolve its name from the corresponding lookup endpoint.

drill_spectral_set.description: The logging set this interval belongs to, as an identity object, or null when the interval is not in a set. Sets let several loggers log the same hole independently.

depth_from.description: Top of this interval, measured ALONG the hole from the collar, in `length_units`.

depth_to.description: Base of this interval, measured ALONG the hole from the collar, in `length_units`.

display_units.description: Units the *_display strings on this record are formatted in, from the project's display preference. Presentation only: the stored values remain in `length_units`.

length_units.description: Units the record's DEPTH and LENGTH values are stored in: `M` (metres) or `FT` (feet). Stored units, not a display preference — read every depth against this.

xyz_from.description: Desurveyed position at `depth_from`, as `[x, y, z]` on the PROJECT LOCAL GRID in metres — not WGS84, and not the record's own `epsg`. Null when the hole has no survey to desurvey against.

xyz_to.description: Desurveyed position at `depth_to`, as `[x, y, z]` on the project local grid in metres. Null when the hole has no survey.

items.description: Nested abundance row — geounit code/label/color + the cell value.

images.description: Attached records, each as an object carrying its id, its natural key and display metadata. Soft-deleted attachments are omitted.

items.description: What is wrong with a stored row. geoDB returns stored data as it is; this marks it so it can be found and corrected.

code.description: `azimuth_out_of_range`: azimuth (or dip direction) is outside 0..360 degrees.; `coordinate_outside_crs`: the coordinate cannot be in its epsg (degrees beyond ±90 latitude or ±180 longitude under EPSG:4326).; `depth_past_hole`: the depth lies beyond the hole's total depth.; `dip_out_of_range`: dip is outside -90..90 degrees.; `interval_upside_down`: depth_from is greater than depth_to (an upside-down interval).; `invalid_geometry`: the stored geometry is not valid (for example a self-intersecting outline).; `missing_epsg`: the record has coordinates but no epsg, so their CRS is unknown.; `negative_value`: a depth, length or total depth is negative.

field.description: The field the warning is about.

data_warnings.description: Present only when this stored row has a problem geoDB can recognise (an upside-down interval, a dip past 90°, coordinates with no CRS…). The row is returned exactly as stored — never fixed or hidden; correct it with an update.

^cf_[a-z0-9_]+$.description: Custom field. Any number of `cf_*` keys may be present: they are the project's user-defined fields, flattened to top level. The set of keys and their types vary BY PROJECT and BY MODEL — discover them at `/api/v2/model-schemas/?project_id=<id>`, never by assuming a fixed set. Values are whatever the customer stored (string, number, boolean or null). Calculated custom fields appear under the same prefix and are read-only.
